{{Nihongo|'''Watatsu Shrine'''|度津神社|Watatsu-jinja}}  is a Shinto shrine in the Hamochiiioka neighborhood of the city of Sado, Niigata.<ref>VisitSado.com, [http://www.visitsado.com/en/01outline/08pt_09/06.shtml  Watatsu Shrine] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304121858/http://www.visitsado.com/en/01outline/08pt_09/06.shtml |date=2016-03-04 }}; retrieved 2012-11-6.</ref> It is the ''[[ichinomiya]]'' of former Sado Province.<ref>[http://eos.kokugakuin.ac.jp/modules/xwords/images/uploads/EOS070712Ab.pdf "Nationwide List of ''Ichinomiya''," p. 2]; retrieved 2012-3-13.</ref> The main festival of the shrine is held annually on the April 23.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Shibuya |first1=Nobuhiro |title=Shokoku jinja Ichinomiya Ninomiya San'nomiya |date=2015 |publisher= Yamakawa shuppansha |isbn=978-4634150867 |language=Japanese}}</ref>

==Enshrined ''kami''==
The primary ''[[kami]]'' enshrined at Watatsu Jinja are:
* {{nihongo|'''Isotakeru-no-Mikoto'''|五十猛命|}}, god shipbuilding and sailing.<ref name="Watatsu Jinja">Kotodamaya.com, [http://www.kotodamaya.com/watatsu-jinja/  "Watatsu Jinja"]; retrieved 2012-11-6.</ref><ref name="books.google.com">Pickens, Stuart D. B. (2004). [https://books.google.com/books?id=BKAhUVqKFhgC&pg=PA372&dq=  ''Sourcebook in Shinto: Selected Documents,'' p. 372].</ref>
*{{nihongo|'''Oyahitsuhime no mikoto'''|大屋津姬命||}}, sister of Isonotakeru
*{{nihongo|'''Tsumatsuhime no mikoto'''|抓津姬命||}}, sister of Isonotakeru

==History==
Located on the island of [[:en:Sado island|Sado]] in the Sea of Japan, the history of Watatsu Shrine is uncertain, as the shrine was completely destroyed by a flood during the Kan'ei era (1624-1643) of the [[:en:Edo Period|Edo Period]].<ref>Sado Travel Guide, [http://www5.ocn.ne.jp/~kagetsu/englishyoyaku/travelguideplace.html#hamochi  "Hamochi"]; 佐渡市 観光課 観光振興係 (佐渡観光振興), 佐渡一ノ宮度津神社 (Sado Ichinomiya Shrine); excerpt, 度津神社の由緒は「延喜式」神名帳（927th year ）に記載されている神社を式内社と言い、当時佐渡の国には九社あり; retrieved 2012-11-6.</ref>   According to shrine tradition, it was founded by the semi-legendary [[Kofun period]] Emperor Chūai (reigned 192–200 AD). Its name appears in the ''[[Engishiki]]'' records compiled in 927 AD, but only as a minor shrine. It was destroyed by a flood in 1470, and rebuilt by the Honma clan, who were rulers of Sado island, in 1472. The shrine appears to have been destroyed repeatedly by floods in 1493, 1533 and 1593, and was merged in 1493 with a  nearby [[Hachiman shrine]]. It is only mentioned as an ''ichinomiya'' in 1678 with the publication the {{nihongo|Shokoku Ichinomiya Pilgrimage Record|諸国一宮巡詣記|Shokoku Ichinomiya Pilgrimage Record}} by Shinto scholar Tachibana Mitsuyoshi. Following the [[Meiji Restoration|Meiji restoration]], with the establishment of State Shinto in 1872, the shrine was classified as a {{nihongo|National shrine, 3rd Rank|国幣小社|[[Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|Kokuhei-shōsha]]}}.<ref name="Shibuya">{{cite book |last1=Shibuya |first1=Nobuhiro |title=諸国神社 一宮・二宮・三宮 |date=2015 |publisher=Yamakawa Publishing Company |isbn=978-4634150867}}{{in lang|ja}}</ref><ref name="Irie">{{cite book |last1=Irie |first1=Koichiro |title=諸国一の宮 |date=2018 |publisher=Idō kyōshitsu Publishing |isbn=978-4901398060}}</ref>

The enshrined ''[[kami]]'' is  {{nihongo|'''Isonotakeru no mikoto'''|五十猛命||}},<ref name="books.google.com"/> the son of [[Susanoo-no-Mikoto]], who is said to have taught people shipbuilding and how to use ships,<ref name="Watatsu Jinja"/> and his two sisters  {{nihongo|'''Oyahitsuhime no mikoto'''|大屋津姬命 ||}} and {{nihongo|'''Tsumatsuhime no mikoto'''|抓津姬命 ||}}<ref name="Shibuya"/>

Each year in late-April, horseback archery (''[[yabusame]]'') takes place at the branch shrine in the town of Hamochi.<ref>[http://eos.kokugakuin.ac.jp/modules/xwords/entry.php?entryID=996  "''Yabusame shinji'',"] ''Encyclopedia of Shinto''; retrieved 2012-11-6.</ref>

The shrine is located about 15 minutes by car from Ogi Port.<ref name="Okada">{{cite book |last1=Okada |first1=Shoji |title=Taiyō no chizuchō 24 zenkoku 'Ichinomiya' meguri |date=2014 |publisher=Heibonsha |isbn=978-4582945614 |language=Japanese}}</ref>
